q: This workstation is designated for visiting staff, isn't it?
answer: Yes, but feel free to use it until someone turns up.
distractors: The designer sent three logo options.
We visited the factory last spring.
zh_q: 這個工作站是指定給來訪同仁用的，對吧？
zh_answer: 對，不過有人來之前你儘管用。
zh_distractors: 設計師寄了三款標誌方案過來。
我們去年春天參觀了工廠。
ex: 附加問句想確認這個座位是否保留給來訪人員。「Yes, but feel free to use it until someone turns up.」先肯定，再補充有人來之前可以先用。「The designer sent three logo options.」的 designer 只是和 designated 發音相近；「We visited the factory last spring.」的 visited 只是和 visiting 相近，講的是參觀工廠。

q: It would be more pragmatic to lease the equipment, wouldn't it?
answer: Especially since we'll only need it for six months.
distractors: At least a dozen people signed up.
The gym equipment is brand new.
zh_q: 設備用租的會比較實際，不是嗎？
zh_answer: 尤其我們只需要用六個月。
zh_distractors: 健身房的器材是全新的。
ex: 附加問句想確認「租設備比較務實」。「Especially since we'll only need it for six months.」表示同意，並補充只需要用六個月這個理由。「At least a dozen people signed up.」的 least 只是和 lease 發音相近，講的是報名人數；「The gym equipment is brand new.」只是重複 equipment，沒有回應該不該用租的。

q: Shall we deploy the update tonight or hold off until the weekend?
answer: The site gets the fewest visitors on Sundays.
distractors: The date on the form is wrong.
Hold on, I'll transfer your call.
zh_q: 更新要今晚就部署，還是延到週末？
zh_answer: 網站星期天的訪客最少。
ex: 二選一：今晚部署或延到週末。「The site gets the fewest visitors on Sundays.」指出星期天訪客最少，暗示週末再做比較好。「The date on the form is wrong.」的 date 只是和 update 發音相近；「Hold on, I'll transfer your call.」的 hold on（稍等）和 hold off（延後）不同，是講電話的用語。

q: Our turnover among sales staff has been unusually high this year.
answer: Maybe it's time we reviewed the incentive plan.
distractors: Turn over the page and sign at the bottom.
The shelf is too high for me to reach.
zh_q: 今年我們業務人員的流動率高得不尋常。
zh_answer: 也許該檢討一下獎勵制度了。
zh_distractors: 請把這頁翻過來，在最下面簽名。
那個架子太高，我搆不到。
ex: 這句話指出業務人員流動率偏高，合適的回應是提出對策或看法。「Maybe it's time we reviewed the incentive plan.」建議檢討獎勵制度來留住人才。「Turn over the page and sign at the bottom.」的 turn over 是「翻頁」，和 turnover（流動率）無關；「The shelf is too high for me to reach.」只是重複 high，講的是架子的高度。

q: Should the proceeds go to the scholarship fund or the community center?
answer: The donors asked us to split them evenly.
distractors: Please proceed to the front desk.
The center is closed on public holidays.

zh_answer: 捐款人要求我們平均分配。
zh_distractors: 中心在國定假日不開放。

q: How do you plan to offset the surge in shipping costs?

distractors: The ship departs from the harbor at dawn.

zh_q: 運費暴漲，你打算怎麼抵銷這筆成本？

zh_distractors: 船在黎明時從港口出發。

q: What accounts for the discrepancy between these two invoices?
answer: One of them doesn't include the delivery charge.
distractors: I opened both accounts at the same bank.
They're in the top drawer of my desk.
zh_q: 這兩張發票的金額為什麼對不起來？

zh_distractors: 我兩個帳戶都開在同一家銀行。
它們在我桌子最上層的抽屜裡。
ex: What accounts for … 是「造成…的原因是什麼」。「One of them doesn't include the delivery charge.」說明差異來自其中一張沒算運費。「I opened both accounts at the same bank.」把 accounts 當成「帳戶」，和問題無關；「They're in the top drawer of my desk.」回答的是東西放在哪裡。

q: Can you authorize this purchase order before you leave today?
answer: Leave it on my desk and I'll look it over.
distractors: The names are listed in alphabetical order.

zh_q: 你今天下班前可以核准這張採購單嗎？
zh_answer: 放在我桌上，我會看一下。
zh_distractors: 名字是照字母順序排列的。
ex: 這是請對方在下班前核准採購單。「Leave it on my desk and I'll look it over.」請對方把單子留在桌上，表示會處理。「The names are listed in alphabetical order.」的 order 是「順序」，和 purchase order（採購單）不同；「The leaves are turning red already.」的 leaves 是「樹葉」，和 leave（離開）無關。

q: Can the new software handle a sudden surge in orders?
answer: It crashed twice during last week's test.
distractors: I ordered the soup and a salad.
Please handle the boxes with care.

ex: 問句問軟體能否應付訂單暴增。「It crashed twice during last week's test.」用「測試時當機兩次」暗示恐怕不行。「I ordered the soup and a salad.」把 order 當成「點餐」；「Please handle the boxes with care.」的 handle 是「搬運」，和問句中「應付、處理」的意思不同，也沒有回答問題。

q: Why is there such a backlog of customer inquiries this week?
answer: Half the support team is away at an offsite workshop.
distractors: Please log back in and try again.
By the end of the week at the latest.
zh_q: 這星期怎麼會積了這麼多客戶詢問沒處理？

ex: Why 問原因。「Half the support team is away at an offsite workshop.」說明人手少了一半，正是案件積壓的原因。「Please log back in and try again.」的 log back 只是和 backlog 聽起來像，講的是重新登入；「By the end of the week at the latest.」回答的是期限，不是原因。

q: Isn't the audit supposed to commence next Monday?
answer: The auditors asked to push it back a week.
distractors: The auditorium seats five hundred people.
The comments were very helpful.
zh_q: 查帳不是應該下星期一開始嗎？
zh_answer: 稽核人員要求往後延一個星期。
ex: 否定問句想確認查帳是否下星期一開始。「The auditors asked to push it back a week.」說明稽核人員要求延後一週，也就是時間改了。「The auditorium seats five hundred people.」的 auditorium（禮堂）只是和 audit 開頭相同；「The comments were very helpful.」的 comments 只是和 commence 發音相近。

q: Do we need to solicit bids from more than one supplier?
answer: Company policy calls for at least three.
distractors: The supplies are in the storage closet.
I bid on a painting at an auction once.
zh_q: 我們需要向不只一家供應商徵求報價嗎？

zh_distractors: 我曾經在拍賣會上競標過一幅畫。
ex: 問句問是否需要向多家供應商徵求投標報價。「Company policy calls for at least three.」說明公司規定至少要三家，等於回答「需要」。「The supplies are in the storage closet.」的 supplies（用品）只是和 supplier 相近，回答的是東西放哪裡；「I bid on a painting at an auction once.」的 bid 是拍賣出價，講的是個人經驗，與問題無關。

q: Ms. Rivera will facilitate the strategy session again, won't she?
answer: She's on leave, so Mr. Chen is filling in.
distractors: The facilities include a pool and a gym.

zh_q: 策略會議這次還是由里維拉小姐主持吧？

zh_distractors: 設施包括游泳池和健身房。

q: Could you gauge the team's interest in a flexible schedule?

zh_distractors: 您的班機從九號登機門出發。

q: Didn't Ms. Novak oversee the regional subsidiary before she transferred here?

q: Does the new attendance policy apply to contractors as well?

q: Are you flying out tonight or staying for the closing reception?

zh_distractors: 那家店再十分鐘就要打烊了。
ex: 二選一：今晚離開或留下來參加閉幕酒會。「My flight isn't until tomorrow afternoon.」說明班機是明天下午，暗示今晚會留下來。「The receptionist is on her lunch break.」的 receptionist（接待人員）只是和 reception（酒會）相近；「The shop is closing in ten minutes.」的 closing 是「打烊」，沒有做出選擇。

ex: 對方報告業績大幅超標的好消息，合適的回應是肯定或稱讚。「The team deserves some recognition for that.」表示團隊值得表揚。「I'd like a price quote for this printer.」的 quote（報價）只是和 quota（額度）發音相近；「The margins on this page are too narrow.」的 margins 是「頁面邊界」，和 by a substantial margin（大幅地）意思不同。

q: Mr. Tanaka's credentials are impressive, but he lacks managerial experience.

ex: 對方評論應徵者資歷好但缺管理經驗，合適的回應是提出解決辦法。「We could pair him with a senior mentor at first.」建議先安排資深導師帶他。「I left my credit card at home.」的 credit card 只是和 credentials 開頭相近；「The manager's office is down the hall.」的 manager 只是和 managerial 相近，講的是辦公室位置。

q: Would you rather present the quarterly metrics yourself or have me do it?

zh_q: 承包商還沒把新的工作站裝好嗎？

q: Did the vendor comply with our revised delivery specifications?

q: The client says there's a discrepancy on the latest invoice.

q: Is Ms. Park going to succeed Mr. Ortiz as regional director?

q: Could you reiterate the main points for those who joined late?

zh_q: 利害關係人對初步的預算數字有什麼反應？
zh_answer: 他們想先看到更詳細的明細，才願意表態。
ex: How did … react 問對方的反應。「They want a more detailed breakdown before they commit.」說明他們還有保留，要看到更細的明細才肯承諾，正是在描述反應。「I figured it out by myself, thanks.」的 figured out（想通）只是和 figures（數字）用了同一個字；「The preliminary round starts at nine.」重複了 preliminary，講的卻是預賽時間。

q: The new expense software isn't as intuitive as I'd hoped.
answer: There's a tutorial video on the staff portal.
distractors: That restaurant is far too expensive.
I hope the weather improves by Friday.
zh_q: 新的費用申報軟體沒有我原本期待的那麼好上手。
zh_answer: 員工入口網站上有教學影片。
zh_distractors: 希望星期五前天氣會好轉。
ex: 對方抱怨新軟體不夠直覺好用，合適的回應是提供協助。「There's a tutorial video on the staff portal.」告訴對方有教學影片可以看。「That restaurant is far too expensive.」的 expensive 只是和 expense 相近；「I hope the weather improves by Friday.」只是重複 hope，講的是天氣。

q: Didn't the board unanimously approve the expansion plan?
answer: Two members voted against it, actually.
distractors: The expansion will add two new floors.
The cutting board is in the kitchen.
zh_q: 董事會不是一致通過擴張計畫了嗎？
zh_answer: 其實有兩位董事投了反對票。
ex: 否定問句想確認「董事會是否全體一致通過」。「Two members voted against it, actually.」指出有兩位投反對票，也就是並非一致通過，糾正了對方的認知。「The expansion will add two new floors.」重複 expansion，講的是擴建內容，沒有回答表決結果；「The cutting board is in the kitchen.」的 board 是「砧板」，和董事會無關。

q: Management has decided to curtail all nonessential travel this quarter.
answer: Then I'll switch my client visit to a video call.
distractors: The curtains in the lobby look new.
A quarter past three would suit me.
zh_q: 管理階層決定這一季要削減所有非必要的出差。
zh_answer: 那我把拜訪客戶改成視訊通話。
zh_distractors: 大廳的窗簾看起來是新的。
ex: 對方告知公司要削減非必要出差，合適的回應是說明自己如何配合。「Then I'll switch my client visit to a video call.」表示會把拜訪改成視訊。「The curtains in the lobby look new.」的 curtains（窗簾）只是和 curtail（削減）發音相近；「A quarter past three would suit me.」的 quarter 是「十五分鐘」，和「季度」意思不同。

q: Is the appraisal meeting in the boardroom or in your office?
answer: Neither, we've moved it online.
distractors: I got approval from my supervisor.
Yes, the office is open on Saturdays.
zh_q: 考核面談是在董事會會議室還是在你的辦公室？
zh_answer: 都不是，我們改成線上進行了。
ex: 二選一問地點。「Neither, we've moved it online.」表示兩個地方都不是，已改成線上，是選擇問句常見的回答方式。「I got approval from my supervisor.」的 approval（批准）只是和 appraisal（考核）發音相近；「Yes, the office is open on Saturdays.」用 Yes 回答選擇問句不合，也只是重複 office。

q: Can you expedite my order? I need it for a presentation on Thursday.
answer: Express delivery will get it to you by Wednesday.
distractors: The expedition lasted three weeks.
The presentation went very well, thank you.
zh_q: 我的訂單可以加急處理嗎？星期四簡報要用。
zh_answer: 用快遞的話，星期三前可以送到您手上。
zh_distractors: 那趟探險持續了三個星期。
簡報進行得很順利，謝謝。
ex: 顧客請對方加快處理訂單。「Express delivery will get it to you by Wednesday.」說明用快遞星期三前可到，趕得上星期四，等於答應了請求。「The expedition lasted three weeks.」的 expedition（探險）只是和 expedite 發音相近；「The presentation went very well, thank you.」重複 presentation，但用過去式講簡報已經結束，和「星期四才要用」不合，也沒有回應請求。

q: Do you think the proposed timeline is viable?
answer: Not unless we get two more developers.
distractors: The time zone difference is eight hours.
The line at the bank was very long.
zh_q: 你覺得提出的時程可行嗎？
zh_answer: 除非再多兩位開發人員，否則不行。
ex: 問句問時程可不可行。「Not unless we get two more developers.」表示除非加人，否則不可行，是有條件的否定。「The time zone difference is eight hours.」的 time zone 只是和 timeline 相近；「The line at the bank was very long.」的 line（隊伍）也只是取 timeline 的後半，內容無關。

q: Will the workshop be held onsite or at an offsite location?
answer: The training room here is being renovated.
distractors: I couldn't find the website.
The workshop lasted about three hours.
zh_q: 研習會在公司內辦，還是在外面的場地辦？
zh_answer: 我們這裡的訓練室正在整修。
zh_distractors: 研習會進行了大約三小時。
ex: 二選一：在公司內或公司外舉辦。「The training room here is being renovated.」說明公司的訓練室在整修，暗示只能在外面辦。「I couldn't find the website.」的 website 只是和 onsite、offsite 發音相近；「The workshop lasted about three hours.」重複 workshop，回答的卻是時間長度，而且用的是過去式。

q: It's imperative that we meet the compliance deadline this Friday.
answer: Then I'll clear my schedule to finish the paperwork.
distractors: Nice to meet you, too.
The appliance store is having a sale.
zh_q: 這星期五的法規遵循期限，我們非趕上不可。
zh_answer: 那我把行程排開，把文件弄完。
ex: 對方強調一定要趕上期限，合適的回應是表示會配合。「Then I'll clear my schedule to finish the paperwork.」表示會空出時間把文件完成。「Nice to meet you, too.」的 meet 是「認識」，和 meet the deadline（趕上期限）不同；「The appliance store is having a sale.」的 appliance（電器）只是和 compliance 發音相近。

q: Does the bank require collateral for a loan of this size?
answer: Not for established customers like us.
distractors: I'm all alone in the office today.
We sat on the river bank for hours.
zh_q: 這種額度的貸款，銀行會要求提供擔保品嗎？
zh_answer: 像我們這種往來多年的老客戶就不用。
zh_distractors: 今天辦公室只有我一個人。
我們在河岸邊坐了好幾個小時。
ex: 問句問銀行是否要求擔保品。「Not for established customers like us.」回答：對我們這種往來已久、信譽良好的客戶不需要。「I'm all alone in the office today.」的 alone 只是和 a loan 發音相近；「We sat on the river bank for hours.」的 bank 是「河岸」，和銀行無關。

q: Do you want the comprehensive report or just a brief summary?
answer: I only have five minutes before my next call.
distractors: The summer schedule starts in June.
Yes, the reporter interviewed him.
zh_q: 你要完整的報告，還是只要簡短的摘要？
zh_answer: 離下一通電話我只剩五分鐘。
zh_distractors: 夏季時刻表六月開始實施。
ex: 二選一：完整報告或簡短摘要。「I only have five minutes before my next call.」表示時間很少，暗示只要摘要。「The summer schedule starts in June.」的 summer 只是和 summary 發音相近；「Yes, the reporter interviewed him.」用 Yes 回答選擇問句不合，reporter（記者）也只是和 report 相近。

q: Is it feasible to consolidate the two warehouses before the fiscal year ends?
answer: Only if we hire extra movers.
distractors: The fees are listed on the last page.
The warehouse is on Harbor Street.
zh_q: 在這個會計年度結束前把兩間倉庫合併，可行嗎？
zh_answer: 除非我們多請一些搬運人員。
ex: 問句問「可不可行」。「Only if we hire extra movers.」是有條件的肯定：多請搬運人員才辦得到。「The fees are listed on the last page.」的 fees（費用）只是和 feasible 開頭的音相近；「The warehouse is on Harbor Street.」重複 warehouse，回答的卻是地點。

q: Could you forward me the blueprints for the new showroom?
answer: The architect hasn't released the final version.
distractors: The show starts at eight tonight.
Go forward two blocks and turn left.
zh_q: 可以把新展示間的藍圖轉寄給我嗎？
zh_answer: 建築師還沒釋出最終版本。
zh_distractors: 往前走兩個街區再左轉。
ex: 這是請對方轉寄藍圖。「The architect hasn't released the final version.」說明最終版還沒出來，暗示現在還沒辦法寄，是合理的間接回答。「The show starts at eight tonight.」的 show 只是和 showroom 相近；「Go forward two blocks and turn left.」的 forward 是「往前」，和「轉寄」意思不同。

q: Where are we going to hold the debrief after the trade show?
answer: It's all in the calendar invitation I sent.
distractors: I'd like a brief summary, please.
We traded shifts last weekend.
zh_q: 商展結束後的檢討會要在哪裡開？
zh_answer: 我寄的行事曆邀請裡都寫了。
zh_distractors: 麻煩給我一份簡短的摘要。
ex: Where 問地點。「It's all in the calendar invitation I sent.」沒有直接說地點，而是請對方看行事曆邀請，是合理的間接回答。「I'd like a brief summary, please.」的 brief（簡短的）只是和 debrief（檢討會）相近；「We traded shifts last weekend.」的 traded（交換）只是和 trade show 用了同一個字。

q: The caterer just called to say the delivery truck broke down.
answer: Did they say how late the food will be?
distractors: I'll take my break at two o'clock.
The call lasted almost an hour.
zh_q: 外燴業者剛打來說送貨車拋錨了。
zh_answer: 他們有說餐點會晚多久到嗎？
zh_distractors: 那通電話講了快一個小時。
ex: 對方通報外燴的送貨車拋錨，合適的回應是追問影響。「Did they say how late the food will be?」追問餐點會延誤多久，切合情境。「I'll take my break at two o'clock.」的 break（休息）只是和 broke down 相近；「The call lasted almost an hour.」只是重複 call，講的是通話時間。

q: The patent application was filed before the deadline, wasn't it?
answer: Our attorney submitted it with a day to spare.
distractors: Please be patient, it won't take long.
The files are in the top cabinet.
zh_q: 專利申請有在期限前送件吧？
zh_answer: 我們的律師提前一天就送出去了。
zh_distractors: 請耐心等一下，不會太久。
檔案放在最上層的櫃子裡。
ex: 附加問句想確認專利申請是否及時送件。「Our attorney submitted it with a day to spare.」表示律師提早一天送出，with a day to spare 是「還有一天的餘裕」，等於肯定。「Please be patient, it won't take long.」的 patient（有耐心的）只是和 patent 發音相近；「The files are in the top cabinet.」的 files 是「檔案」，和 filed（提出申請）不同，回答的是東西放哪裡。

q: When do you expect the auditors to finish reviewing the ledger?
answer: It depends on how quickly we send the missing receipts.
distractors: In the accounting office on the third floor.
Yes, the audio was much clearer this time.
zh_q: 你估計稽核人員什麼時候會審完總帳？
zh_answer: 要看我們多快把缺的收據送過去。
zh_distractors: 對，這次的音訊清楚多了。
ex: When 問時間。「It depends on how quickly we send the missing receipts.」沒給確切日期，但說明完成時間取決於補交收據的速度，是合理的間接回答。「In the accounting office on the third floor.」回答的是地點；「Yes, the audio was much clearer this time.」用 Yes 回答 When 問句不合，audio（音訊）也只是和 auditors 發音相近。

q: Aren't you going to attend the shareholders' meeting this afternoon?
answer: I'm sending my deputy in my place.
distractors: I intend to buy a new laptop.
Good afternoon, may I take your order?
zh_q: 你今天下午不去參加股東會嗎？
zh_answer: 我會派我的副手代替我去。
zh_distractors: 午安，可以幫您點餐了嗎？
ex: 否定問句想確認對方是否出席股東會。「I'm sending my deputy in my place.」表示會派副手代替，也就是自己不去。「I intend to buy a new laptop.」的 intend 只是和 attend 發音相近；「Good afternoon, may I take your order?」只是重複 afternoon，是服務生的招呼語。

q: Why don't we designate one person to coordinate the booth setup?
answer: Ms. Ito has offered to take that on.
distractors: Because the boots were too tight.
I set up my new phone last night.
zh_q: 我們何不指定一個人來統籌攤位佈置？
zh_answer: 伊藤小姐已經主動說要接下這件事了。
zh_distractors: 我昨晚把新手機設定好了。
ex: Why don't we … 是提出建議。「Ms. Ito has offered to take that on.」表示已經有人自願負責，take on 是「承擔」，是合理的回應。「Because the boots were too tight.」把它當成問原因來回答，boots 也只是和 booth 發音相近；「I set up my new phone last night.」的 set up 是「設定手機」，沒有回應建議。

q: Couldn't we mitigate the delay by adding a second shift?
answer: That would entail hiring a lot more staff.
distractors: The relay race starts at ten.
Please shift the table to the left.
zh_q: 我們不能加開第二班來減輕延誤嗎？
zh_answer: 那樣勢必得多請很多人。
ex: 否定問句是在提議加開一班來減少延誤。「That would entail hiring a lot more staff.」指出這樣勢必要多請很多人，對提議表示保留。「The relay race starts at ten.」的 relay 只是和 delay 發音相近；「Please shift the table to the left.」的 shift 是「移動」，和「班次」意思不同。

q: Don't we need the director's approval to exceed the budget?
answer: Only for expenditures over five thousand dollars.
distractors: The direction signs are confusing.
He succeeded on his first try.
zh_q: 超出預算不是需要總監核准嗎？
zh_answer: 超過五千美元的支出才需要。
zh_distractors: 那些方向指標讓人看不懂。
他第一次嘗試就成功了。
ex: 否定問句想確認超出預算是否要總監核准。「Only for expenditures over five thousand dollars.」說明只有超過五千美元的支出才需要，是有條件的肯定。「The direction signs are confusing.」的 direction 只是和 director 相近；「He succeeded on his first try.」的 succeeded 只是和 exceed 發音相近。

q: Please make sure the visitors sign in before entering the premises.
answer: I'll have the log sheet ready at the front desk.
distractors: The sign on the door says closed.
The entry fee is five dollars.
zh_q: 請務必讓訪客在進入場區前先簽到。
zh_answer: 我會把登記表準備好放在櫃台。
zh_distractors: 門上的牌子寫著休息中。
ex: 這是交代對方要讓訪客先簽到。「I'll have the log sheet ready at the front desk.」表示會在櫃台備好登記表，等於答應照辦。「The sign on the door says closed.」的 sign 是「牌子」，和 sign in（簽到）不同；「The entry fee is five dollars.」的 entry 只是和 entering 相近，講的是入場費。

q: I noticed the fire exit on the second floor is blocked by boxes.
answer: That's against the safety code. I'll have them moved.
distractors: The exit interview is scheduled for Monday.
The notice was posted yesterday.
zh_q: 我發現二樓的逃生出口被箱子堵住了。
zh_answer: 那違反安全規範，我會請人搬走。
ex: 對方指出逃生出口被堵住，合適的回應是表示會處理。「That's against the safety code. I'll have them moved.」說明這違反安全規範，並會請人搬走。「The exit interview is scheduled for Monday.」的 exit interview 是「離職面談」，和逃生出口無關；「The notice was posted yesterday.」的 notice（公告）只是和 noticed 相近。

q: Why don't we outsource the payroll processing to an outside firm?
answer: I'm not sure that would be cheaper in the long run.
distractors: Because the outside door was locked.
Please press the button firmly.
zh_q: 我們何不把薪資作業外包給外面的公司？
zh_answer: 長期來看，我不確定那樣會比較省錢。
ex: Why don't we … 是提出建議，不是問原因。「I'm not sure that would be cheaper in the long run.」對建議表示保留，是合理的回應。「Because the outside door was locked.」把它當成問原因的 Why 來回答，也只是重複 outside；「Please press the button firmly.」的 firmly（用力地）只是和 firm（公司）相近。

q: Would you mind if I worked offsite on Friday?
answer: As long as you can still join the team call.
distractors: The sightseeing bus leaves at nine.
It works much better now.
zh_q: 我星期五不進公司、在外面工作，你介意嗎？
zh_answer: 只要你還是能參加團隊的電話會議就行。
ex: Would you mind if … 是在徵求許可。「As long as you can still join the team call.」是有條件的同意：只要還能參加團隊會議就可以。「The sightseeing bus leaves at nine.」的 sightseeing 只是和 offsite 發音相近；「It works much better now.」的 works 是「運作」，和 worked（工作）意思不同，也沒有回應請求。

q: The payroll deductions look higher this month, don't they?
answer: The new insurance premium took effect on the first.
distractors: Payday is the twenty-fifth of each month.
He's much taller than his brother.
zh_q: 這個月薪水的扣款看起來比較多，對吧？
zh_answer: 新的保險費一號開始生效了。
zh_distractors: 發薪日是每個月二十五號。
ex: 附加問句想確認「這個月扣款變多了」。「The new insurance premium took effect on the first.」說明保費調整已生效，等於同意並解釋原因。「Payday is the twenty-fifth of each month.」講的是發薪日，沒有回應扣款變多；「He's much taller than his brother.」的 taller 只是和 higher 意思相近，講的是身高。

q: Would you prefer the ergonomic chair or the standing desk?
answer: Actually, I was hoping to get both.
distractors: I can't stand waiting in long lines.
The chairperson will speak first.
zh_q: 你比較想要人體工學椅，還是站立式辦公桌？
zh_answer: 其實我本來希望兩樣都有。
ex: 二選一：人體工學椅或站立式辦公桌。「Actually, I was hoping to get both.」表示兩個都想要，是選擇問句常見的回答。「I can't stand waiting in long lines.」的 can't stand 是「受不了」，只是用了 stand；「The chairperson will speak first.」的 chairperson（主席）只是含有 chair，內容無關。

q: I heard the merger won't be finalized until next fiscal year.
answer: Really? I thought the board had already signed off.
distractors: The finalists will be announced tomorrow.
It's physically demanding work.
zh_q: 我聽說合併案要到下個會計年度才會定案。
zh_answer: 真的嗎？我以為董事會已經核准了。
zh_distractors: 決賽入圍名單明天公布。
ex: 對方轉述合併案延後定案的消息，合適的回應是表示意外或追問。「Really? I thought the board had already signed off.」表達驚訝，並說出自己原本的認知。「The finalists will be announced tomorrow.」的 finalists（決賽入圍者）只是和 finalized 相近；「It's physically demanding work.」的 physically 只是和 fiscal 發音相近。

q: Will the board endorse the plan to outsource customer support?
answer: Several members have serious reservations.
distractors: Support staff are available around the clock.
We boarded the plane an hour late.
zh_q: 董事會會支持把客服外包的計畫嗎？
zh_answer: 有好幾位董事相當有疑慮。
zh_distractors: 我們晚了一小時才登機。
ex: 問句問董事會會不會支持。「Several members have serious reservations.」的 reservations 是「疑慮、保留意見」，暗示不一定會通過。「Support staff are available around the clock.」只是重複 support，沒有回答董事會的態度；「We boarded the plane an hour late.」把 board 當成「登機」，與問題無關。

q: The dress code for the awards dinner is formal attire, right?
answer: That's what it says on the invitation.
distractors: The code for the door is four two one.
I need to replace a flat tire.
zh_q: 頒獎晚宴的服裝規定是正式服裝，對吧？
zh_answer: 邀請函上是這麼寫的。
zh_distractors: 我得換掉一個沒氣的輪胎。
ex: 句尾的 right 想確認晚宴要穿正式服裝。「That's what it says on the invitation.」表示邀請函上就是這樣寫，等於肯定。「The code for the door is four two one.」的 code 是「密碼」，和 dress code（服裝規定）不同；「I need to replace a flat tire.」的 a tire 和 attire 發音幾乎一樣，講的卻是輪胎。

q: Which contractor did the facilities team shortlist for the lobby renovation?
answer: They haven't narrowed it down yet.
distractors: The contract is short, only two pages.
In the lobby, next to the reception desk.
zh_q: 大廳整修工程，設施組把哪一家承包商列入候選名單？
zh_answer: 他們還沒篩選出來。
ex: Which contractor 問是哪一家承包商入圍。「They haven't narrowed it down yet.」表示還沒篩選出名單，是合理的間接回答。「The contract is short, only two pages.」的 contract（合約）和 short 只是和 contractor、shortlist 聽起來像；「In the lobby, next to the reception desk.」回答的是地點。

q: Wasn't the software rollout scheduled for the first of the month?
answer: Testing uncovered a few bugs, so it's been delayed.
distractors: The rolls are fresh from the oven.
It's the first door on your left.
zh_q: 軟體不是預定一號上線嗎？
zh_answer: 測試時發現了幾個錯誤，所以延後了。
ex: 否定問句想確認軟體是否原定一號上線。「Testing uncovered a few bugs, so it's been delayed.」說明測試發現錯誤，所以延後了。「The rolls are fresh from the oven.」的 rolls（麵包捲）只是和 rollout 相近；「It's the first door on your left.」只是重複 first，回答的是位置。

q: You're accountable for the inventory figures, aren't you?
answer: Only for the east warehouse.
distractors: The accountant retired last year.
The inventor won a national award.
zh_q: 庫存數字是由你負責的，對吧？
zh_answer: 我只負責東倉的部分。
zh_distractors: 那位會計師去年退休了。
那位發明家得了全國性的獎項。
ex: 附加問句想確認對方是否要對庫存數字負責。「Only for the east warehouse.」表示只負責東倉的部分，是部分肯定。「The accountant retired last year.」的 accountant（會計師）只是和 accountable 相近；「The inventor won a national award.」的 inventor（發明家）只是和 inventory（庫存）發音相近。

q: Would you be able to mediate between the two department heads?
answer: I'd rather someone neutral from human resources did it.
distractors: The medium size should fit you.
The apartment is on the top floor.
zh_q: 你可以居中調解這兩位部門主管嗎？
zh_answer: 我寧可讓人資部立場中立的人來做。
ex: 這是請對方出面調解兩位部門主管。「I'd rather someone neutral from human resources did it.」婉拒，並建議由人資部立場中立的人來做，是合理的回應。「The medium size should fit you.」的 medium 只是和 mediate 發音相近；「The apartment is on the top floor.」的 apartment 只是和 department 發音相近。

q: Should I reallocate the funds to marketing or leave them in research?
answer: That's at the finance director's discretion.
distractors: He left the office about an hour ago.
The market is open until six.
zh_q: 這筆經費我該改撥給行銷部，還是留在研發部？
zh_answer: 那要由財務總監決定。
zh_distractors: 他大約一小時前離開辦公室了。
ex: 二選一：經費改撥行銷或留在研發。「That's at the finance director's discretion.」的 at someone's discretion 是「由某人決定」，表示這不是我們能定的，是合理的間接回答。「He left the office about an hour ago.」的 left 是「離開」，和問句的 leave（留著）意思不同；「The market is open until six.」的 market（市場）只是和 marketing 相近。

q: Isn't it mandatory to back up client files to the offsite server?
answer: Yes, and the system does it automatically every night.
distractors: I'll be back in ten minutes.
The server brought us the wrong dishes.
zh_q: 客戶檔案不是規定要備份到異地伺服器嗎？
zh_answer: 對，而且系統每天晚上都會自動備份。
zh_distractors: 服務生幫我們上錯菜了。
ex: 否定問句想確認是否強制要備份到異地伺服器。「Yes, and the system does it automatically every night.」肯定，並補充系統每晚自動備份。「I'll be back in ten minutes.」的 back 是「回來」，和 back up（備份）不同；「The server brought us the wrong dishes.」的 server 是「服務生」，和伺服器無關。

q: Shall I book a private room, or is the main dining area fine?
answer: We'll be discussing some confidential figures.
distractors: I've read that book twice.
The main course comes with a salad.
zh_q: 要我訂包廂嗎？還是坐一般用餐區就可以？
zh_answer: 我們會討論一些機密數字。
ex: 二選一：訂包廂或坐一般用餐區。「We'll be discussing some confidential figures.」表示要談機密內容，暗示需要包廂。「I've read that book twice.」把 book 當成名詞「書」，和「預訂」無關；「The main course comes with a salad.」只是重複 main，講的是餐點，沒有做出選擇。

q: Are we going to renew the lease or look for new premises?
answer: We've already started viewing other buildings.
distractors: He made a promise to call back.
Yes, the news was on this morning.
zh_q: 我們要續租，還是另外找新的辦公場所？
zh_answer: 我們已經開始看其他大樓了。
zh_distractors: 對，今天早上有播那則新聞。

q: Shouldn't we assess the risks before we initiate the project?
answer: The consultants are already working on that.
distractors: The access road is closed today.
The rice was a little dry.
zh_q: 啟動專案之前，我們不是應該先評估風險嗎？
zh_answer: 顧問已經在做這件事了。
ex: 否定問句是在建議先評估風險。「The consultants are already working on that.」表示顧問已經在評估了，等於同意並說明現況。「The access road is closed today.」的 access 只是和 assess 發音相近；「The rice was a little dry.」的 rice 只是和 risks 發音相近，內容無關。

q: What's causing the intermittent connectivity problems on the fourth floor?
answer: A technician is coming to look into it this afternoon.
distractors: My connecting flight leaves in forty minutes.
Yes, it's on the fourth floor.
zh_q: 四樓連線時斷時續，是什麼原因造成的？
zh_answer: 今天下午會有技術人員來查。
zh_distractors: 我的轉機班機四十分鐘後起飛。
ex: What's causing 問原因。「A technician is coming to look into it this afternoon.」表示原因還不清楚、要等技術人員來查，是合理的間接回答。「My connecting flight leaves in forty minutes.」的 connecting（轉機）只是和 connectivity（連線）相近，講的是班機；「Yes, it's on the fourth floor.」用 Yes 回答 What 問句不合，也只是重複 fourth floor。

q: Attendance at the outreach event was lower than expected, wasn't it?
